governingRule: An OCW explanation does not establish a theory's historical priority, experimental verification, current research consensus, or completeness. Original research papers and experimental collaborations remain the appropriate authorities for those separate claims.
linkingRule: theoryIds and formulaIds are navigational crosswalks to existing catalog records, not modifications, new graph edges, or claims that OCW originally published those formulas.
reuseRule: Link to MIT-hosted OCW course and notes; preserve citation and create original commentary and self-worked calculations. No course PDFs, figures, or transcribed lecture text are republished.

lessons.title: Two-state Hilbert spaces, spin and time evolution
locators: Chapter 7, section 2, printed p. 3, Eqs. (2.8) and (2.10) (spin Hamiltonian and time evolution)
lessons.usefulAddition: Use a two-dimensional subspace as a concrete example of amplitudes, relative phase and unitary motion. Explain how a spin-1/2 measurement basis changes predicted probabilities.
lessons.selfWorkedCheck: For a state (|up>+|down>)/sqrt(2) under H=-gamma B S_z, the relative phase changes with angular rate gamma B; the probabilities in the z basis stay one-half each.
lessons.assumptions: Uniform time-independent magnetic field along z; isolated spin; unit-normalized state; sign of gamma is conventional.
nonClaims: A qubit abstraction does not assert that its carrier has no other physical degrees of freedom.
Unitary dynamics does not itself describe a measurement outcome or any experimental qubit fidelity.

lessons.title: Tensor products, Bell pairs and reduced states
lessons.module: Chapter 8 — Multiparticle States and Tensor Products
locators: Chapter 8, section 1, printed p. 3, Eq. (1.6) (composite-state dimension)
Chapter 8, sections 2–3, printed pp. 9–10, including Eq. (3.52) (separability/Bell-state example)
lessons.usefulAddition: Distinguish an entangled joint pure state from the local mixed state of either subsystem; tie the tensor-product rule to the meaning of a Bell pair.
lessons.selfWorkedCheck: For |Phi+>=(|00>+|11>)/sqrt(2), the 2x2 coefficient determinant is 1/2, so the state is not a product; tracing out either qubit gives I/2.
lessons.assumptions: Two distinguishable two-level systems for the example; normalized pure joint state and standard computational basis.
nonClaims: Entanglement alone is not a demonstrated Bell-inequality violation without specifying measurements and statistics.
A maximally mixed local state cannot transmit information faster than light.

lessons.title: Nondegenerate perturbation theory and an exact comparison
locators: Chapter 1, section 1, printed p. 1, Eq. (1.2) (H(lambda)=H0+lambda delta H)
Chapter 1, section 1, printed p. 8, Eqs. (1.1.36)–(1.1.37) (nondegenerate energy corrections)
lessons.usefulAddition: Demonstrate why the denominator E_n^(0)-E_m^(0) controls the small-coupling approximation, using an exactly diagonalizable two-state Hamiltonian.
lessons.selfWorkedCheck: For H0=diag(0,Delta), V=epsilon sigma_x and Delta>0, the ground energy is [Delta-sqrt(Delta^2+4(lambda epsilon)^2)]/2; at small |lambda epsilon|/Delta it is -(lambda epsilon)^2/Delta plus higher-order terms.
lessons.assumptions: Nondegenerate unperturbed levels; Delta>0; Hermitian perturbation and |lambda epsilon|<<Delta.
nonClaims: The expansion is not reliable near degeneracy without a changed method.
An algebraic worked check is not an observed energy shift in a laboratory.

lessons.title: Gauge-covariant derivatives and Yang–Mills field strength
locators: Lecture 3, printed p. 2, Eqs. (14) and (16) (D_mu and commutator field strength)
Lecture 3, printed p. 3, Eqs. (19) and (21) (gauge action/field-strength components)
lessons.usefulAddition: Explain which sign convention is used, why the commutator generates nonlinear terms in a non-Abelian field, and how the Abelian limit differs.
lessons.selfWorkedCheck: Under D_mu=partial_mu-i g A_mu, [D_mu,D_nu]=-i g F_munu with F_munu=partial_mu A_nu-partial_nu A_mu-i g[A_mu,A_nu]. For commuting A_mu the commutator term vanishes.
lessons.assumptions: Hermitian matrix-valued generators, D_mu=partial_mu-i g A_mu and the lecture's Lie algebra conventions; normalization of Tr(T^a T^b) must be supplied to compare action prefactors.
nonClaims: Changing D_mu sign convention changes corresponding F_munu sign conventions; formulas must be reconciled before modifying existing records.
This is pedagogical gauge-theory mathematics, not a new experimental finding or replacement for primary Yang–Mills literature.

lessons.title: What three-qubit repetition codes correct—and what they do not
lessons.lecturer: Peter Shor (course); lecture scribed by Dah-Yoh Lim
locators: Lecture 16, printed pp. 1–2 (three-qubit bit-flip repetition code and need to handle phase errors separately)
lessons.usefulAddition: Give a specific syndrome calculation and contrast correctable single-X errors with an undetected logical-Z action in the repetition code.
lessons.selfWorkedCheck: Encode alpha|0>+beta|1> as alpha|000>+beta|111>. A physical X on qubit 2 reverses both Z1Z2 and Z2Z3 parities; a Z on qubit 1 changes alpha|000>+beta|111> to alpha|000>-beta|111> and leaves both parity checks +1.
lessons.assumptions: Ideal encoding, measurement and correction; a single Pauli error in the exercise; the specific code has bit-flip distance three but does not protect an arbitrary qubit from an arbitrary single-qubit error.
nonClaims: Encoding is a linear isometry, not cloning an unknown quantum state.
The elementary repetition code does not independently establish practical fault tolerance or the general Knill–Laflamme criterion.
